key_insight: Answer Set Programming (ASP) can compactly encode and solve decade-scale power grid planning problems with rich topological and combinatorial constraints, producing optimal multi-year upgrade schedules that preserve supply continuity and service quality.
problem_solved: How to plan long-term (multi-year to decade) grid expansions and upgrades under complex topology, operational, and deployment constraints (while meeting sustainability and demand changes) without violating service continuity despite combinatorial explosion of possibilities.
method: Model the long-horizon planning problem as an ASP program that encodes network topology, component choices, temporal deployment steps, and operational constraints.
Use ASP solvers to search and optimize feasible upgrade schedules across scenarios, enforcing continuity and combinatorial/topological constraints exactly.
Support scenario-based and incremental planning (cost/benefit trade-offs, multiple objectives) via solver-guided enumeration and optimality criteria.
impact: Demonstrates a symbolic, interpretable alternative to purely numerical optimization for large combinatorial infrastructure planning; AI/ML practitioners can combine ASP-based planners with ML forecasts for robust, verifiable long-term decision support.
visual_elements: Multi-year timeline showing staged upgrades and preserved supply continuity (Gantt-style)
Pipeline diagram: data/forecasts → ASP model (constraints & objectives) → solver → candidate plans
Network diagram overlayed with constraint icons (topology constraints, capacity, redundancy) to show feasible vs infeasible modifications
Comparison chart (e.g., solution quality vs. computation time) contrasting ASP with MILP/heuristics
paper_title: Long-term Power Grid Planning via Answer Set Programming
paper_authors: Antonio Ielo, Francesco Doria, Sandra Castellanos-Paez, Marco Maratea, Francesco Percassi
